verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The C_d formula is literal: λ(D + c_η)(1 − λ)/(β²(λ − h + c_η)) with D = 1/2 − h, c_η = geometricSource, β = decay = 1/2 − λ, λ − h + c_η = equilibriumNumerator — `derivativeCoefficient` is character-for-character that quotient. The expression 2R_b − C_d ∂_{ξ_b}R_b is `idealDirection` exactly. Three routine rewritings. (i) The `+ o(1)` is made quantitative: |w − idealDirection| ≤ componentConstant(P,m,A)·coneRate λ with coneRate λ = λ + √λ(1+log(1/λ)) → 0 (coneRate_tendsto_zero). (ii) `C_d ≤ 2 + o(1)` is rendered as the concrete C_d ≤ 2001/1000 under the explicit thresholds λ ≤ 10^-5 and h ≤ λ·10^-5, rather than as a limit; that is the numerical form the later margin 2.001·1.2 ≤ 2.41 of the next display needs. (iii) R_b in `idealDirection` is mainRatio = amp·mainPulse(λy), the main pulse without the exponentially small end-bump corrections; the paper likewise sets those aside ('Apart from exponentially small end bumps'). The passage from the exact coefficient (1 − λ)/β on R_b in `mainDirection` (PulseCone.lean:1039) to the paper's 2 costs directionMainErrorConstant·λ (mainDirection_ideal_error, PulseCone.lean:1585), absorbed in the same o(1), since (1 − λ)/(1/2 − λ) = 2 + 2λ/(1 − 2λ).
